answer: A velvet‑soft reputation ledger records every agent’s signed task proofs and timestamps, forming a tamper‑evident chain. When a new node joins, a willow‑shaped challenge‑matrix randomly assigns it a set of honeypot queries whose answers are known only to a rotating gale of verifiers; any mismatch flags the node and triggers a stake burn. An attacker must generate unique valid signatures for each challenge, paying computational work proportional to the number of fake identities, making a Sybil surge prohibitively expensive.
